title: Scottish nobles sign the Declaration of Arbroath
summary: Scottish barons sent a letter to Pope John XXII asserting Scotland's independence and their right to choose their own king. It is dated at Arbroath Abbey.
reason: England refused to accept Robert the Bruce as king, and the pope had excommunicated him, so the Scots sought papal recognition.
significance: It became one of the most famous early statements of national sovereignty and of a king ruling by consent.
place: Arbroath Abbey, Arbroath, Scotland, United Kingdom
